body.p: Upon entry of this Response, claims 1, 3-16, and 18-22 are pending in the present patent application. Claims 1, 3, 6, 8, 15, 16, and 19 are amended. Claims 21 and 22 are newly added and contain no new matter. Claim 2 is cancelled without waiver, prejudice, or disclaimer. Claim 17 was previously cancelled. Applicant reserves the right to present these cancelled claims, or variants thereof, in continuing applications. Reconsideration of the presently pending claims in view of the following remarks is respectfully requested.
I. Summary of Telephone Interview

Applicant would like to thank Examiner Acosta for time spent with Applicant's representative, Marlena F. Burt (Reg. No. 68750), during telephone interview on October9, 2024. During the interview, the rejection of the claims and potential proposed amendments were discussed. While no agreement was reached, Examiner Acosta provided suggestions for amendments which have been included in this response.
II. Claims 1-16 and 18-20 Satisfies the Requirements of 35 U.S.C. § 112(b)

On page 2 of the Office Action, claims 1-16 and 18-20 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the Applicant regards as the invention. Applicant respectfully submits that claims 1-16 and 18-20, as amended, satisfies the requirements of 35 U.S.C. § 112(b). Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 1-16 and 18-20 be withdrawn.
III. Claims 1, 3-16, and 18-20 Are Patentable over the Cited References

On page 3 of the Office Action, claims 1-4, 11-16, 18 and 20 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as allegedly being unpatentable over Burrows, et al. (US Pub. 2013/0206907, hereinafter Burrows) in view of Banfield, et al. (US Pub. 2018/0251222, hereinafter Banfield). On page 8 of the Office Action, claims 5-8 and 19 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as allegedly being unpatentable over Burrows) in view of Banfield and further in view of Swain (US Pub. 2014/0123571, hereinafter Swain). On page 10 of the Office Action, claim 9 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as allegedly being unpatentable over Burrows in view of Banfield and further in view of Haney, et al. (US Pat. 6,079,6691, hereinafter Haney). On page 11 of the Office Action, claim 10 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as allegedly being unpatentable over Burrows in view of Banfield and further in view of Seibt (US Pub. 2014/154758, hereinafter Seibt). Claim 2 has been cancelled, thereby rendering the rejection of claim
2 moot.

In order to establish a prima facie case of obviousness under 35 U.S.C. § 103, the Examiner must provide a factual basis to support the legal conclusion of obviousness by showing that each and every element of the claim is described or suggested by the prior art or would have been obvious in view of the prior art. See In re Fine, 837 F.2d 1071, 1073-74 (Fed. Cir. 1988); Ex Parte Wada and Murphy, Appeal 2007-3733 (B.P.A.I. 2008); see also, KSR Int'l v. Teleflex, Inc., 550 U.S. 398, 411 (2007) (claim deemed obvious to one of ordinary skill where all claim elements were disclosed in the cited prior art references). In addition, "[r]ejections on obviousness grounds cannot be sustained by mere conclusory statements; instead, there must be some articulated reasoning with
some rational underpinning to support the legal conclusion of obviousness." KSR Int'/,
550 U.S. at 418 (quoting In re Kahn, 441 F.3d 977, 988 (Fed. Cir. 2006)). Applicant
respectfully requests that the rejections of claims 1, 3-16, and 18-20 be withdrawn for at
least the following reasons.
To begin, Applicant respectfully submits that the combination of cited references
fails to show or suggest each and every element of amended claim 1. Claim 1, as
amended, recites:
1. A lavatory unit for an aircraft cabin,
wherein the lavatory unit comprises a perimeter wall that separates

an internal space of the unit from space external to the unit, and is configurable between an able-bodied configuration and a Person of Reduced Mobility (PRM)-accessible configuration, wherein the PRM- accessible configuration of the lavatory unit accommodates a PRM in a
wheelchair and allows for a transfer from the wheelchair to the toilet,
wherein in the able-bodied configuration the lavatory unit has a first
internal floor space and there is a cabin floor space external to the lavatory
unit,
wherein the lavatory unit is expandable into the PRM-accessible
configuration in which the lavatory unit is expanded to have a second internal floor space, the second internal floor space encompassing a region
of the cabin floor space
wherein the perimeter wall comprises a moveable wall
assembly, and in the able-bodied configuration the moveable wall assembly is in a retracted configuration, and the moveable wall assembly is moveable into an expanded configuration to expand the
lavatory unit into the PRM-accessible configuration; and
wherein in the able-bodied configuration a user can access the

first internal floor space via a door opening in the perimeter wall, the door opening having an effective width and wherein movement of the moveable wall assembly from the retracted configuration to the expanded configuration increases the effective width of said door
opening to enable a PRM to access the internal floor space.
(Emphasis added). In rejecting claim 1, the Office Action alleges that the combination of
Burrows and Banfield discloses the elements of claim 1, as previously presented.
Applicant notes that claim 1 has been amended to include the above emphasized
elements of claim 1. According, Applicant respectfully submits that the combination of cited references fails to show or suggest each and every element of amended claim 1.

By way of example only, Fig. 4 of the present application shows an example lavatory unit in the able-bodied configuration, with the door 110 open to allow an able- bodies user to access the interior of the lavatory unit via a door opening 140 (see page 19 lines 19 to 21 of the PCT application as published). Opening 140 can be closed by door 110. As is described at pg. 20 lines 3 to 19 of the PCT application and as is apparent from Figs 4, 5A and 5B, displacement of moveable wall assembly 152 expands the lavatory unit to the PRM-accessible configuration shown in Fig 5a and 5b. Fig 5b shows sliding panel 128 slid back into the unit and door 110 pivoted open to allow a PRM to access the interior of the lavatory unit via a door opening 148 which has a greater effective width than opening 140 in Fig. 4.

Unlike an able-bodied user, a PRM in a wheelchair will typically be unable to turn sideways to fit through a narrower doorway. Having a lavatory unit in which movement of the moveable wall assembly from the retracted configuration to the expanded configuration increases the effective width of the door opening to allow for PRM accessibility, without the need for a wider door in the retracted configuration (and a correspondingly wide unit - undesirable when space is at a premium in the aircraft cabin). Additionally or alternatively, the use of a moveable wall assembly as required by claim 1 may provide this combination of space-efficiency and accessibility in a mechanically simple and/or user friendly way.
For at least the following reasons, Applicant respectfully submits that the combination of cited references fails to show or suggest each and every element of claim

Burrows discloses a lavatory unit in which a portion of wall 16 can be rotated to increase the internal area of the unit. As acknowledged by the Office Action, Burrows fails to explicitly teach the PRM-accessible configuration of the lavatory unit accommodates a PRM in a wheelchair as required by claim 1. FIG. 3/3A of Burrows is reproduced below:

To the extent Fig. 3/3A discloses an opening associated with door 26, the size of that doorway does not change. Accordingly, Burrows also fails to disclose wherein in the able-bodied configuration a user can access the first internal floor space via a door opening in the perimeter wall, the door opening having an effective width and wherein

movement of the moveable wall assembly from the retracted configuration to the expanded configuration increases the effective width of said door opening to enable a PRM to access the internal floor space, as required by claim 1.

Banfield also fails to disclose "wherein in the able-bodied configuration a user can access the first internal floor space via a door opening in the perimeter wall, the door opening having an effective width and wherein movement of the moveable wall assembly from the retracted configuration to the expanded configuration increases the effective width of said door opening to enable a PRM to access the internal floor space," as required by claim 1. Accordingly, Banfield cannot remedy the deficiencies of Burrows in this regard.

Swain is concerned with two-toilet lavatory units. As shown and described in e.g. Fig. 7 to 10, [0049] and [0059] of Swain, divider door 18 is folded to combine first and second lavatory interiors 27, 28. To provide access to the combined first and second lavatory interiors 27, 28 the first and second lavatory doors 31, 32 are also opened and the centre post 40 is unlatched and slid to the left.

To the extent Swain discloses a unit that is configurable between an able-bodied configuration and a PRM-accessible configuration, that unit comprises both the first and second lavatory interiors 27, 28 as the structure of both areas is required to define the internal floor area in the PRM-accessible configuration. The footprint of the two-toilet

lavatory unit of Swain does not expand and accordingly Swain fails to disclose the lavatory unit is expanded to have a second internal floor space, the second internal floor space encompassing a region of the cabin floor space. It follows that Swain cannot disclose a moveable wall assembly that is moveable into an expanded configuration to expand the lavatory unit as required by claim 1. As a consequence, Swain cannot disclose wherein movement of the moveable wall assembly from the retracted configuration to the expanded configuration increases the effective width of said door opening to enable a PRM to access the internal floor space as required by claim 1. Or, to put it another way, Swain fails to disclose that moving the moveable wall assembly to expand the lavatory unit also increases the effective width of the door opening.

Further, the approach of Swain only works in a two-lavatory unit, so it's not clear how it would be implemented in the single-lavatory units of Burrows as shown in Fig. 3/3A. Where Burrows does disclose two-lavatory units (e.g. Fig. 7/7A), their layout appears to be incompatible with the approach of Swain (e.g. because the doorways of the two lavatories are not aligned in a way that would allow their widths to be combined).

For at least these reasons, Applicant respectfully submits that the combination of cited references fails to show or suggest each and every element of amended claim 1. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claim 1 be withdrawn. Insofar as claim 15 recites elements similar in scope to those of claim 1, Applicant respectfully submits that the rejection of claim 15 be withdrawn for at least similar reasons, to the extent applicable. In addition, Applicant respectfully submits that the rejection of claims 3-14, 16, and 18-20 be withdrawn for at least the reason that claims 3-14, 16, and 18-20 depend from claim 1 or 15.
IV. Newly Added Claims 21 and 22

Applicant notes that claims 21 and 22 are newly added and contain no new matter. Insofar as claim 21 recites elements similar in scope to those of claim 1, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 21 is allowable for at least similar reasons, to the extent applicable. In addition, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 22 is allowable for at least the reason that claim 22 depends from claim 21. In addition, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 22 is allowable for at least the reason that claim 22 requires that the lavatory unit is a single-toilet lavatory unit which is not applicable to the combination of cited references.
V. No Waiver

Applicant's arguments and amendments are without prejudice, waiver, or disclaimer. Applicant has not addressed each specific rejection of the dependent claims because Applicant submits that the independent claims are allowable over the documents of record, as discussed above. Applicant has not acquiesced to any such rejection and reserves the right to address the patentability of any additional claim elements in the future.

It is requested that all outstanding objections and rejections be withdrawn and that this application and all presently pending claims be allowed to issue. If the Examiner has any questions or comments regarding this Response, the Examiner is encouraged to telephone the undersigned counsel of Applicant.
